# Bureaucracy As Death

**Aliases:** bureaucracy as institutional death, death by bureaucracy, dead institution, office logic.

> **Fast answer:** Bureaucracy as death is Jiang's term for an institution that survives by draining away the openness, genius, discovery, responsibility, and lived reality that once made it alive. The office keeps moving, but the institution can no longer imagine its own failure or renewal.

## What Jiang Means

Jiang's bureaucracy model is not only red tape. Bureaucracy manufactures problems so it can sell solutions, processes people into compliance, protects its own procedures, and keeps threat surfaces alive because the office needs a reason to exist.

The death is institutional and spiritual. A living mission turns into pension logic, rule maintenance, and self-justifying threat management. The system still operates, but operation is no longer life.

## How To Use This Term

Use this term when Jiang is diagnosing an institution that preserves itself by replacing living judgment with procedure, threat surfaces, and compliance.

Do not use it for mere administrative inconvenience.
